title: Preserve exact owner-issued Case identifiers across Case picker, Timeline, Search Job and run comparison
goal: Repair the integrated Case selector contract: never trim owner-issued Case IDs in the local analyst browser, so two authorized IDs that differ only by surrounding spaces remain distinct through Timeline, Search Job and two-Case comparisons.
invariants: An owner-issued Case ID is an opaque exact selector, not a presentation string; no client-side whitespace normalization or aliasing.
Case picker must never silently open a different Case, Timeline, Search Job, local provenance or comparison when two IDs differ only in whitespace.
Existing server-side principal, tenant/environment, Case, Timeline, and typed-source authorization remains authoritative; no client trust, new IAM, persistence or Evidence mutation.
security_properties: For every Case-selection path, compare asynchronous context revisions against the exact unchanged Case ID string.
Use exactly the selected Case ID in authorized Timeline GET, normalized Search Job POST and cross-Case selection; distinct owner IDs must remain distinct.
Existing denial, case-change invalidation and foreign-source protections remain unchanged; no extra requests, source data, bearer or tenant leakage.

migration.rationale: Client-only exact selector fidelity; no persisted canonical Case identifier or backend schema change.

rollback.strategy: Revert only browser selector normalization change; server-side Case owner and discovery predicates remain unchanged.
verification: Existing Case picker, Timeline and Search Job authorization tests remain unchanged.

inputs: Canonical CAP-INV-110 Case and Timeline navigation and CAP-INV-101 Case picker transitions.
Existing backend validHTTPCaseSelector accepts valid owner-issued IDs with nonblank surrounding spaces; client trim() previously silently selected a different ID.
Previously independently integrated and CI-green PR #134 preserves owner authentication and transient CAP-INV-008 comparison.

Existing first-party Go analyst UI asset security test used brittle literal marker `option.textContent = id`; replace only that marker with the equally inert unambiguous JSON escaped visual textContent contract while preserving option.value opaque wire identity.
outputs: Exact Case ID string preserved through Case picker → Timeline GET and Search Job POST; no silent aliasing.
Two Case IDs differing by trailing spaces remain valid distinct Case choices in the local comparator.
Browser regression tests, exact-HEAD cross-OS Actions, bounded handoff documenting partial synthetic nature.
Case selector dropdown renders whitespace-significant owner IDs unambiguously; matching Go UI static contract test is updated within this task, no backend authorization change.
acceptance_tests: Case discovery with both 'case-disk' and ' case-disk ' allows opening the exact selected original ID without silently changing it.
Executing an authorized completed normalized Search Job submits exactly the selected owner Case ID; moving to the other ID invalidates all stale results and provenance.
A two-Case comparison retains 'case-disk' and 'case-disk ' as separate owner selections.
Full Linux Go/Node browser and macOS/Windows Go suites and mandatory unchanged security coverage gate on exact SHA.

Go asset contract accepts the first-party dropdown rendering `option.textContent = JSON.stringify(id).replace(/ /g, "\\u0020")` and still rejects raw HTML injection or switching to client-authorized source lookup; Node tests prove both visible distinct labels and byte-exact option values.

performance_budget.rationale: Only remove string normalization on local Case identifiers, no additional network or data enumeration.

definition_of_ready: CAP-INV-110/101 case selector contract and CAP-INV-002 Search Job have existing first-party backend, fixed identity predicate and CI-green integration PR #134, with no product decision required.
Git parent PR #134 exact frozen SHA is a dependency, not the engineering parent; new work is a bounded browser-facing R2 fix.
definition_of_done: Exact owner-issued Case IDs retained in actual Case picker, Timeline, Search Job and cross-Case comparison workflows.
Case changes invalidate prior authorized Search Job and provenance controls, no metadata leak or wrong-Case silent reroute.
Exact-head runtime and mandatory engineering security workflows verified, release/draft/parent approvals kept distinct.
